Fix numbers stored as text, N/A and blanks in a CSV

A column will not sum when a few stray values turn it into text. Find those values first, decide what each one means (zero, missing or negative), and only then convert. Converting before deciding is how a dash becomes a zero and quietly drags your average down.

Updated 4 November 2026. Examples on this page were run for real; the data in them is made up.

What the stray values usually are

We ran this made-up column through a conversion that strips symbols and commas. The right-hand column is what each value should become, and the reasoning is the part that needs a human.

Value in the fileBecomesWhy
1,234.501234.5Thousands separator removed
₹2,0002000Currency symbol removed. Keep the currency somewhere if it varies.
(450)-450Brackets are the accounting way to write a negative
12 12Trailing space
N/AmissingNot a number, and not a zero
(empty)missingNothing was recorded
-missing or 0Depends on the source. Ask.

Missing and zero are not the same thing

Take three amounts: 100, 200 and a dash. If the dash means zero, the average is (100 + 200 + 0) / 3 = 100. If it means "not recorded", the average is (100 + 200) / 2 = 150. Same file, a 50 percent difference, no error message either way. Decide per column, write the rule down, and apply it to the whole column.

Decimal commas, thousands commas and lakh grouping

In the US and UK, 1,234.50 is one thousand two hundred thirty-four and a half. In much of Europe the same number is written 1.234,50. If your CSV is in a European format and you strip commas, you get 1.23450, a number about a thousand times too small, and nothing complains. We checked: replacing the dots with nothing and the comma with a dot turns 1.234,50 into 1234.5, which is right only if you know the file is European.

A bare 1,234 is the hardest case. It is 1234 in a US file and 1.234 in a European one. Look for a value in the same column that settles it, such as one with two decimals or both separators. In India you will also see lakh grouping, 1,23,456.00, which is 123456. Stripping the commas handles that one correctly.

Fix it in Excel or Google Sheets

  • Green triangle. If Excel shows a small green triangle in the corner, choose Convert to Number. It only handles the easy cases.
  • Multiply by 1. Type 1 in a cell, copy it, select the column, Paste Special, Multiply. Values that are not numbers will show an error, which is useful: those are your stray values.
  • Non-breaking spaces. Numbers copied from web pages can carry them, and they stop conversion. =SUBSTITUTE(A2,CHAR(160),"") removes them.
  • Trailing minus. Some exports, SAP among them, write a negative as 450-. Excel will not read that as negative. Move the sign to the front before converting.

Do not convert codes that look like numbers

A postal code, phone number, account number or product code is a label, not a quantity. Convert 00123 to a number and it becomes 123. The leading zeros are gone for good. If you will never add or average a column, leave it as text.

A safe order

  1. Keep a copy of the original file.
  2. Find the values that are not plain numbers (the multiply trick above lists them).
  3. For each kind, decide: negative, zero, missing, or ask the source.
  4. Convert the column.
  5. Check that the count of numbers plus the count of missing values equals the number of rows, and that the total is sensible.

Questions people ask

Why won't my column of numbers add up in Excel?

At least one value in it is text, such as N/A, a dash, a value with a trailing space or a non-breaking space. Excel then treats the cells as text and SUM skips them. Find the odd values first, then convert.

Should a dash or N/A be zero?

It depends on what the source meant. Zero means a recorded amount of nothing, missing means nothing was recorded. They give different averages, so decide per column and ask the source if unsure.

How do I convert (450) to -450?

Brackets are the accounting way to write a negative. Strip the brackets and put a minus sign in front, or use a tool step that reads brackets as negatives. Check the preview afterwards.

How can I tell 1.234,50 from 1,234.50?

Look at the other values in the column. A value with both separators, or a decimal part of exactly two digits after a comma, shows the format. Check with the source for anything ambiguous like 1,234.
